explanation: The I47V mutation reduces darunavir binding through loss of critical van der Waals contacts in the protease flap region. Isoleucine's larger branched side chain (26.7 Å³ larger) creates optimal hydrophobic packing interactions with darunavir's nonpolar surface at the minimal 2.2 Å ligand distance, whereas valine's smaller methyl branch cannot maintain these favorable van der Waals contacts, resulting in a slight energetic penalty. The reduction in hydrophobicity (-0.3 units) at this flap position also diminishes the favorable desolvation effect that normally accompanies darunavir binding, collectively weakening the interaction by ~0.1 kcal/mol.
